The section to write, as it stands:

## Evidence

The transport office counted 240 boardings in the pilot week, compared with 160 in the earlier observation week. The shuttle therefore caused a 50 percent increase in student attendance. This result sounds decisive when I write it that way. Still, boardings are trips, and one rider can appear in the count several times. The two observation weeks also landed on different points in the semester. I want the numbers to earn their place in this paragraph rather than act like a badge that makes the argument official. The rider survey helps describe who answered, but it cannot tell us what every student needed.



The next section opens with: ## Recommendation - I would keep the route running while checking who can actually use it. The driver I spoke with called the last stop 'the long way home,' and that phrase stayed with me. It catches something the total number of rides misses: access has a shape as well as a size. Next term, the campus could count unique consenting riders, record missed connections, and invite comments from students who never board. This is a modest recommendation. I prefer a modest claim I can explain to a big claim that disappears when someone asks how we counted.
